nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense for the third quarter of 2026 was $1.7 billion , an increase of 6.8% from the same period in 2025 . The increase was

primarily driven by higher average balances in short-term Consolidated obligations, partially offset by lower market interest rates. For

context, interest income increased 6.1% over the same period in 2025 .

Lower interest rates reduced funding costs by $225.6 million , while higher funding volumes increased funding costs by $336.6 million

compared to the third quarter of 2025 . The aggregate cost of funds declined to 373 basis points in the third quarter of 2026 from 425

Our funding mix changed during the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025 , reflecting increased reliance on

floating-rate CO bonds and CO discount notes and a reduced proportion of fixed-rate CO bonds. CO discount notes funded 42.3% of

average earning assets in the third quarter of 2026 , compared to 38.3% in the third quarter of 2025 .

net.heading: Net Income
net.text:
Interest income from advances is the principal source of revenue. Other sources of revenue are interest income from investment debt

securities, liquidity trading securities, mortgage loans in the MPF and MAP portfolio, securities purchased under agreements to resell

and federal funds sold. Fair value gains and losses on liquidity trading securities and equity investments also impact net income. The

primary expense is interest paid on Consolidated obligation debt. Other expenses are primarily compensation and benefits, operating

expenses, our share of operating expenses of the Office of Finance and the FHFA, voluntary contributions, and affordable housing

program assessments on net income. Other significant factors affecting our net income include the volume and timing of investments

in mortgage-backed securities, prepayments of advances, charges due to debt repurchased, gains and losses from derivatives and

hedging activities, and earnings from investing our shareholders’ capital.

Net interest income.heading: Table 9.2 Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
(a) Total Interest Income and Total Interest Expense — See Tables 9.6 and 9.8 and accompanying discussions

Net interest income before the provision for credit losses was $214.5 million for the third quarter of 2026 , an increase of $2.6 million ,

or 1.2% , compared to the third quarter of 2025 . The slight increase primarily reflected higher average interest-earning asset balances,

partially offset by lower market interest rates. Average interest-earning assets increased to $196.0 billion in the third quarter of 2026

from $ 161.5 billion in the prior-year period. The average yield on earning assets declined by 58 basis points year over year. The

decline in yields was driven primarily by advances, including overnight, short-term, and variable-rate advances that repriced to lower

Net interest spread was 24 basis points in the third quarter of 2026 and 30 basis points in the third quarter of 2025 . Net interest margin,

which measures net interest income as a percentage of average interest-earning assets, was 43 basis points in the third quarter of 2026 ,

compared to 52 basis points in the prior-year period.

lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
